chunks: And Sāfi Al-Barqi narrated from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever visits Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) for three consecutive years, without a break, on the fifteenth of Sha'bān, his sins will be forgiven.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq or Imam al-Husayn depending on context, here referring to the one being visited)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting Imam Husain on the 15th of Sha'ban for three years?
ai.summary: Transmitted by Ṣāfī al-Barqī from Imām al-Ṣādiq (a.s.), this hadith emphasizes the enduring spiritual efficacy of consistent devotion, linking the intercession of Imām al-Ḥusayn (a.s.) with divine forgiveness for sustained piety. The requirement of three consecutive years without break underscores the importance of steadfastness (istiqāmah) in maintaining a living connection with the Ahl al-Bayt, transforming a ritual act into a mechanism for comprehensive spiritual purification.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 4. Sāfi Al-Barqi narrated that: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (s.a.a.w.)) said:
The sins of those who go to the Ziyārah of Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Ḥusain (a.s.)) on the fifteenth of Sha’bān for three consecutive years without a break will be forgiven.
